correctness.rationale: For all m,n>=2, explicit symmetric-difference neighborhoods of the three two-token vertex types give independent necessary-and-sufficient open-neighborhood tests: pure-pair choices edge-cover all rows or all columns; mixed-pair choices occupy all but at most one row and one column. Inclusion-exclusion enumerates each class by size and factorization follows from the bipartition. Minimum supports are classified as minimum edge covers and long-coordinate injective placements; their counts are respectively matching/P3 counts and Stirling surjections. Standalone adjacency-derived coefficientwise comparisons match nine parameter pairs, including five independently brute-forced all-subset graphs. Computation is only a check, not an infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General reductions can algorithmically enumerate total dominating sets of an arbitrary finite graph, but do not by themselves assert the explicit all-m,n factorization, multiplicities and comparison. The rook-graph total-domination result concerns the Cartesian product of cliques; that graph has mn vertices, unlike F_2(K_mn) with binomial(m+n,2) vertices. No stronger checked theorem states the claimed formula as a corollary.

originality.rationale: 2025 token-graph domination work studies stars and complete hosts; October 2026 primary work on the same biclique family derives ordinary, not total, domination. Older papers define total-domination polynomials or give reductions, without an identified full explicit token-biclique factorization. General polynomial computability does not supply the exact all-coefficient formula or minimum-set census. Real primary full texts and actual published-record searches were compared; priority remains open to hidden equivalents.
residual_risks: Older or unindexed sources may have independently obtained the factorization under symmetric-square or hypergraph edge-cover language.

value.rationale: Complete all-cardinality enumeration for a natural infinite two-parameter family of token graphs, with two transparent combinatorial factors and complete optimizer classification and multiplicities. It distinguishes ordinary and total domination precisely in the parity/boundary cases. A graph-order-only bound or the published ordinary domination number does not imply the full polynomial.
